linked_issues.title: Four copies of the same HTTP wrapper have drifted apart

source.description:
We have four near-identical _http.py wrappers (payments, shipping, tax, notifications). They were copy-pasted and have drifted: different timeouts, different attempt counts, different logging.

This replaces all four with meridian.http.HttpClient. Per-service behaviour moves into config/http.yaml so the differences are visible in one place instead of spread across four modules. Call sites change one import and one call each; the public functions keep their signatures.

No behaviour change intended - this is a refactor. Lockfiles and generated clients are regenerated in the last commit.

coverage.note: Core and supporting hunks were read in full. Lockfiles and regenerated clients were reduced to their version and symbol deltas.
limitations: docs/assets/http-topology.png is binary and was not analysed.
poetry.lock and clients/ts/pnpm-lock.yaml were read as dependency deltas only, not line by line.
gen/pb/shipping_pb2.py was read far enough to identify which messages changed, not decoded.
The call-site files were read as a group after the first three matched the same two-line shape.

story.headline: Four copied HTTP wrappers collapse into one client, and the retry rules change while they do.

beats.label: Was
beats.text: Four packages each carried a copy of `_http.py`, drifted apart in timeout and retries.

beats.label: Now
beats.text: One `HttpClient`, with the per-service numbers moved into `config/http.yaml`.

beats.label: Watch
beats.text: The retry rules are not a merge of the four. They are new.

intent_delta.stated: Replace four copied _http.py wrappers with one HttpClient and move per-service settings into config/http.yaml. No behaviour change intended.

also_does.summary: Retries seven status codes instead of two, plus three transport errors that used to raise.
Adds a single-step checkout path behind a new flag, enabled for 5% of customers.
Refreshes 14 Python packages including a protobuf major bump, 2 npm packages, and CI Node 18 to 20.
Raises retry_attempts and enables jitter in the Windows collection agent, which shares no code here.

behavior.summary: The retry loop is not the same loop: it catches transport exceptions that used to propagate, matches five more status codes, and sleeps a random interval.

deltas.summary: Transport exceptions are caught and retried instead of propagating on the first failure.
The retryable status set grows from {502, 503} to seven codes including 429 and 500.
The delay becomes a random draw from an exponential ceiling rather than a constant.
Attempt budgets change per service: notifications 2 to 5, shipping 2 to 4, tax 2 to 3.

steps.why: The whole PR is this file plus the decision to call it everywhere. The retry loop is where the refactor stops being a refactor.

annotations.text: Seven status codes. The wrappers retried two.
New category: transport failures are now retryable, where the wrappers let them propagate.
A timeout here means the request may already have been delivered; the retry re-sends it.
Applies to every method, so POSTs are retried on 429 and 500 as well.
The delay is drawn from step 3's helper rather than read from a constant.

checks.title: Connection and timeout errors are now retried, not raised
checks.why: The wrappers wrapped a bare `requests.post`, so `ConnectionError` and `Timeout` reached the caller at once. `HttpClient` catches all three and retries.
checks.question: Are `authorize`, `capture`, `schedule_payout` and `book` idempotent at the provider?

checks.title: The retryable status set grows from two codes to seven
checks.why: 429, 408, 425, 500 and 504 join 502 and 503. A 429 used to surface at once; it is now retried up to the service's attempt budget.
checks.question: How does your rate-limited upstream respond to a retried 429?

checks.title: Attempt budgets rise for three of the four services
checks.why: config/http.yaml sets notifications to 5 attempts where the wrapper used 2, shipping to 4, tax to 3. With the wider status set, worst-case wall time grows.
checks.question: Do the new worst-case call times fit inside your own request timeout?

checks.title: Single-step checkout ships enabled at 5%
checks.why: `enable_single_step_checkout` is `enabled: true, percentage: 5`, routing flagged customers to `create_single_step` instead of `create_from_cart`.
checks.question: Was a 5% checkout rollout part of the plan for this deploy?

checks.title: poetry.lock adds tenacity 8.5.0, which nothing here imports
checks.why: The new client implements its own retry loop. `tenacity` appears as a direct lockfile entry, and no file in this diff imports it.
checks.question: Where does `tenacity` enter the tree, if no file here imports it?

checks.title: protobuf crosses a major version, 4.25 to 5.27
checks.why: The bump is paired with a regenerated `shipping_pb2.py`. Descriptors built by the 4.x runtime share a global pool with these, so mixed versions in one interpreter matter.
checks.question: Does any process in your fleet load 4.x descriptors in the same interpreter?

checks.title: Retry timing becomes non-deterministic
checks.why: `decorrelated_jitter` draws uniformly from `[0, exponential(attempt)]`, replacing a fixed 0.25 to 1.0 second wait. Simultaneous retries no longer align.
checks.question: Do your latency alerts or load tests assume a fixed retry interval?

checks.title: Generated clients expose a RetryHint with no server route
checks.why: The regenerated protobuf and all three orval modules gain `RetryHint`, and orders.ts gains a `/orders/{orderId}/retry-hint` operation. No handler appears here.
checks.question: Which service is meant to serve `/orders/{orderId}/retry-hint`?

checks.title: A vendored file was edited rather than re-vendored
checks.why: `third_party/httpstub/__init__.py` says to re-vendor with scripts/vendor.sh. This diff edits it directly and moves the recorded version from 0.4.2 to 0.5.0.
checks.question: Does `scripts/vendor.sh` still reproduce `third_party/httpstub` byte for byte?

checks.title: The Windows collection agent gets more retries and jitter
checks.why: config/windows-agent.ini moves retry_attempts from 2 to 3 and adds retry_jitter. That agent deploys separately from this service and shares none of this code.
checks.question: Who owns the Windows collection agent's deploy schedule?

# max_attempts counts the first try, so 3 means one call and two retries.
Every outbound call goes through `meridian.http.HttpClient`. There is one
implementation and one place where retry behaviour is decided.
`config/http.yaml` holds a `default` block and a per-service override. A service
| `max_attempts` | Counts the first try. `3` means one call and two retries. |
Idempotency is the caller's problem. The client retries on the status codes in
`RETRY_STATUSES` and on connection, timeout, and chunked-encoding errors, which
means a POST can be sent more than once.
